executiveSummary.headline: Fix Core Meeting Facts Before Treating the Peer Lead as Progress
executiveSummary.lead: Wyndham San Diego Bayside ranks first in its five-hotel Wyndham Rewards set, but 13.6% consideration and 34.8% scenario presence show a substantial absolute visibility gap. Management should treat the rank as relative context—not proof of strong visibility—and first repair the official meeting and operating facts that planners and automated systems rely on.
executiveSummary.metricsNote: AI Consideration is the share of comparable monitored answers mentioning the hotel; Scenario Presence is the share of eligible traveler-need scenarios where it appeared; Certified Peer Position compares only the certified five-hotel set. Presence does not equal bookings, revenue, or traveler exposure.

themes.title: Visible and Machine-Readable Facts Conflict
themes.what: The homepage shows blank meeting-stat placeholders, and two Hotel JSON-LD blocks publish opposing check-in/check-out pairs: 11:00/16:00 versus 15:00/11:00.
themes.whyItMatters: These are verified official-page defects. One hotel-approved operating fact set should replace blanks and conflicts before broader visibility work, because planners and automated systems need consistent basics.

themes.title: The Meetings Page Supplies the Repair Standard
themes.what: The official meetings page states 27,000 square feet and names rooms including the 10,384-square-foot Pacific Ballroom, giving the agency a concrete basis for reconciliation.
themes.whyItMatters: The task is not to invent a meetings proposition. It is to align homepage modules, structured data, room facts, and inquiry paths to a signed sales inventory.

themes.title: Technical and Competitive Signals Remain Investigations
themes.what: A Node probe received Cloudflare 403 responses while browser access worked, and ADP observed Hotel del Coronado displacement without establishing why.
themes.whyItMatters: Neither signal proves an outage, crawler block, or content cause. Bounded, documented partner review should precede any security change or public competitive positioning claim.

priorities.action: GM and agency: repair homepage facts and Hotel schema in 2–3 weeks
priorities.desiredOutcome: One accurate operating and meeting fact set

priorities.action: Sales and agency: reconcile named rooms and capacities within 30 days
Agency and security partner: investigate Cloudflare behavior
Commercial team: review displaced scenarios and factual distinctions

executiveSummary.successLooksLike: Homepage statistics, operational times, named meeting rooms, capacities, and structured data agree with a hotel-signed source of truth; technical and competitive questions have documented decisions.
executiveSummary.closing: Wyndham San Diego Bayside’s peer lead is useful context, but the business opportunity is to raise low absolute consideration from a cleaner foundation: accurate operating facts, complete meeting statistics, and a consistent 27,000-square-foot planner story.

actions.whatWeFound: The homepage leaves meeting-stat values blank. Two Hotel JSON-LD graphs conflict—check-in 11:00/check-out 16:00 versus check-in 15:00/check-out 11:00—while official meetings content states 27,000 square feet.
actions.whyItMatters: Guests, planners, and automated systems should receive one approved set of basic facts. Correcting the conflict protects information accuracy; it does not guarantee more AI mentions or bookings.

Agency populates or removes empty homepage statistic modules.

Archive before-and-after page and schema evidence.

actions.headline: Investigate Cloudflare Access for Intended Crawlers
actions.priorityWhy: A bounded Node probe received 403 responses, but browser-based retrieval worked.
actions.whatWeFound: Automated Node requests to the homepage and robots target received Cloudflare 403 responses, while browser and WebFetch access succeeded. This is not proof of a public outage or universal crawler block.
actions.whyItMatters: The agency should establish whether intended search and AI crawlers receive official content before changing security rules. Investigation protects both accessibility and site security.
recommendedSteps: Open a Cloudflare review with timestamps and user agents.
Confirm the intended robots policy from an approved environment.
Compare WAF behavior for intended crawlers and ordinary automation.
Retest after any hotel-approved rule change.
actions.timeframeNote: Timing is proposed and requires accountable-owner agreement.

completionCriteria.investigationCompleted: A reproducible access matrix documents client, region, URL, status, and expected policy.
completionCriteria.correctionSubmitted: If a mismatch is confirmed, a hotel-approved Cloudflare ticket identifies the narrow rule adjustment.
completionCriteria.correctionVerifiedLive: Agreed clients successfully retest named URLs, or expected denials are documented with rationale.
completionCriteria.noChangeRequired: Valid if the security partner confirms intended crawlers are served and the Node result is environment-specific; decision memo is filed.

actions.hotelApprovalNotes: Do not alter WAF or bot-management rules without hotel and security-partner approval.

changesOrInvestigation: Inspect Cloudflare event logs for the probe window.
